template_adherence.title: ADR 0003: Why did we create a datetime relative component?
template_adherence.context: The ADR explains the need to create a custom datetime relative component to display humanized "time ago" dates in the `<cc-deployments>` components. It discusses the previous use of moment.js and its drawbacks, such as size and lack of tree shaking.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The decision drivers include the need for a small-sized component, short output strings, standard-based implementation when possible, proper handling of weeks, i18n support, and compatibility with browsers including Safari 12+. Concerns about size, output length, API usability, and i18n support influenced the decision.
template_adherence.decision: The decision was to create a custom datetime relative component with features like auto-update every 10 seconds, title attribute with human date, handling only past dates, using `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with a dumb fallback for Safari 12+, and a custom i18n system. This approach results in a small, efficient, and standard-based solution.
template_adherence.consequences: The consequence is a lightweight component (<1.5 KB min+gzip) that produces short, clear output, supports weeks, and works across required browsers. It avoids the drawbacks of existing libraries and components, such as large size, long output, or unclear i18n handling. However, it requires maintaining a custom implementation and fallback logic.

template_adherence.title: ADR 0004: Why do we wrap `<input>` and `<textarea>` in a `div.wrapper` and puts styles on this wrapper?
template_adherence.context: We started by adding styles directly on `<input>` and `<textarea>` (including styles for states like `disabled`,  `:focus`,  `:hover`...). We chose not to wrap text in multiline `<textarea>` and remove the scrollbar.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The behaviour of padding/margin in Chrome/Safari is not the same as Firefox when the text does not wrap. We want the Firefox behaviour (where the margin/padding are not part of the scrollable zone).
template_adherence.decision: Move all styles to a `div.wrapper` (including `:focus` and  `:hover`). This allowed us to listen to some events directly on this wrapper and simplified the computation of the auto height when multiline.
template_adherence.consequences: By moving styles to the wrapper, the styling and event handling became more consistent across browsers, and the auto height computation for multiline inputs was simplified. However, this introduces an additional DOM element which might have minor performance or complexity implications.

alternatives.description: Continue styling `<input>` and `<textarea>` directly without wrapping them in a `div.wrapper`.
pros: No additional DOM elements are introduced.
Simpler HTML structure.
cons: Inconsistent padding/margin behavior across browsers.
More complex event handling and styling for states like `:focus` and `:hover`.
Difficulties in computing auto height for multiline inputs.

alternatives.description: Use JavaScript to normalize styles and behaviors across browsers without adding a wrapper.
pros: No additional DOM elements.
Potentially consistent behavior across browsers if implemented correctly.
cons: Increased complexity in JavaScript code.
Potential performance overhead.
Maintenance burden.

More code required just for layout purposes.

template_adherence.title: ADR 0008: Why an event called `requestimplicitsubmit`?
template_adherence.context: The ADR explains the problem of implementing implicit form submission behavior in web components using shadow DOM, which is currently not supported due to browser limitations and spec immaturity. template_adherence.decision_drivers: The decision is influenced by the need to support implicit submission behavior in forms, limitations of shadow DOM isolation, the immaturity of related web standards (AOM, FACE), team size constraints, and the desire to maintain accessibility and codebase stability.
template_adherence.decision: The team decided to implement a custom event `cc-input-text:requestimplicitsubmit` emitted by the `<cc-input-text>` component to signal implicit submission requests, instead of using light DOM or waiting for spec improvements.
template_adherence.consequences: This decision allows the component to signal implicit submission events in a way compatible with current browser limitations and team constraints. However, it requires users of the component to listen for the custom event and handle form submission manually. Future reconsideration is possible when accessibility issues are addressed or new components are created to handle submission logic.

Better accessibility support as per ING's approach with LitElement and slots.
cons: Requires significant code changes impacting existing codebase.
Not feasible for a small team (~1 person) at this time.
Dependent on spec improvements that are not yet ready.

alternatives.description: Implement a custom event to signal implicit submission requests.
pros: Does not require major codebase changes.
Works around shadow DOM limitations.
Allows custom handling of submission events.

cons: Requires users to listen and handle the custom event manually.
Not a native browser behavior, so may require additional documentation and developer awareness.

template_adherence.title: ADR 0009: How we use the new Storybook CSF and docs page?
template_adherence.context: The ADR describes the context of the Web Components project starting in March 2019, the initial setup with Storybook v5.0.x using `@storybook/html`, and the way stories were created and documented. It also details the limitations and practices used before migrating to newer Storybook features.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include the need to upgrade Storybook to latest 5.3.x, migrate from `@storybook/html` to `@storybook/web-components`, move from `storiesOf()` to Component Story Format (CSF), and transition from addon notes to addon docs with docs page and MDX files. Other drivers include improving story authoring, story reuse, story naming, navigation organization, and documentation quality.
template_adherence.decision: The decision was to migrate Storybook from `@storybook/html` to `@storybook/web-components`, adopt CSF for story authoring, and move from addon notes to addon docs. They created helpers like `makeStory()` and `enhanceStoriesNames()` to ease story creation and naming. They also decided to split stories into smaller units for better docs integration and to keep some markdown documentation as `.stories.mdx` files. template_adherence.title: Introducing HTML in translation strings
template_adherence.context: The ADR addresses the challenge of safely including whitelisted HTML tags within translation strings in an internationalization (i18n) system. The current system returns unsafe HTML strings that require sanitization by the templating library, but the goal is to allow certain HTML tags in static translation parts while escaping HTML in parameters, maintaining isolation from the templating system.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The decision is influenced by the need for security (preventing XSS), isolation/decoupling from the templating system, ease of implementation, size of the solution, and the ability to whitelist specific HTML tags and attributes. The solution should also be compatible with existing build and testing workflows.
template_adherence.decision: The chosen solution is to have the i18n system return either a string or a sanitized DocumentFragment. Static parts of translation strings can include whitelisted HTML tags and attributes, sanitized using a custom small implementation inspired by DOMPurify but lighter. Parameters are escaped using DOM TextNode behavior. This approach maintains decoupling from templating systems like lit-html, ensures security by escaping parameters, and allows trusted HTML in static parts via a sanitize template tag function.
template_adherence.consequences: Positive consequences include improved security by escaping parameters, maintaining isolation from templating systems, and a small, testable sanitization implementation. Negative consequences include the solution only working in DOM-enabled environments (browsers, not Node.js), and the potential for developer mistakes if the sanitize function is not used properly, though this falls back to safe escaping. The solution may complicate build-time checks for HTML misuse in translations.

alternatives.description: The 'trust translation strings' solution where the i18n system sanitizes and trusts its own output, requiring the templating system to trust the HTML strings and use unsafe directives.
pros: Centralizes sanitization in i18n system
Allows use of whitelisted HTML tags in translations
cons: Templating system must trust i18n output, increasing XSS risk if mistakes occur
Requires complex build-time checks to ensure sanitization
Breaks isolation between i18n and templating systems

alternatives.description: The 'return lit-html templates' solution where i18n returns lit-html TemplateResults instead of strings.
pros: Leverages lit-html's built-in escaping and trust model
Avoids need for unsafe directives in components
cons: Breaks decoupling between i18n and templating system
lit-html accepts more than regular HTML, complicating whitelisting
Does not fit requirement to whitelist/filter tags and attributes strictly

alternatives.description: The 'return DOM' solution where i18n returns sanitized DocumentFragments, maintaining decoupling and security.
pros: Maintains isolation from templating systems
Allows strict whitelisting and filtering of HTML tags and attributes
Parameters are safely escaped
Small, testable implementation
Works with multiple templating solutions
cons: Only works in DOM-enabled environments (not Node.js)
Requires developers to use sanitize template tag function correctly
Build-time checks for misuse are harder to implement

template_adherence.title: ADR 0011: Sorting CSS declarations
template_adherence.context: The ADR discusses the motivation and problem of manually sorting CSS declarations inside LitElement based components, which was error-prone and inconsistent. It aims to automate the sorting of CSS declarations alphabetically to improve consistency, conflict detection, and readability.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include the need for consistent CSS declaration order, ease of finding properties, triggering merge conflicts when necessary, and the technical feasibility of automating the sorting process within JavaScript files using LitElement's css tagged template literals.
template_adherence.decision: The decision was to implement an automated sorting of CSS declarations using ESLint with a custom rule that detects and fixes unsorted CSS inside LitElement components. The approach avoids Babel due to formatting issues and uses synchronous PostCSS plugins for sorting, specifically the 'postcss-sorting' plugin, which was found to be synchronous and easy to configure.
template_adherence.consequences: The consequence is improved consistency and maintainability of CSS declarations in LitElement components. The ESLint-based solution allows automatic fixing without disturbing other code formatting. However, some linked CSS properties may be separated due to alphabetical sorting. The approach also opens questions about integrating other tools like Prettier or stylelint for further checks.

alternatives.description: Using Babel to parse and transform JavaScript files to sort CSS declarations.
pros: Babel provides AST transformation capabilities.
Allows direct manipulation of JavaScript source code.
cons: Babel's AST transformation does not preserve original code formatting well.
Resulted in small annoying style modifications in JavaScript parts, which was undesirable.

alternatives.description: Using ESLint with a custom rule to detect and fix unsorted CSS declarations.
pros: ESLint supports fix feature that preserves untouched code parts.
Easier to implement and maintain.
Better integration with existing linting workflows.
cons: Only supports parameter-less tagged template expressions currently.
Requires writing custom ESLint rule.

alternatives.description: Using PostCSS plugins like 'css-declaration-sorter' for sorting CSS declarations.
pros: Powerful CSS parser and transformer.
Existing plugins for sorting CSS declarations.
cons: Some plugins are asynchronous, which is incompatible with ESLint fix feature.
Some plugins require hacky workarounds to be synchronous.
Issues with unknown CSS properties handling.

alternatives.description: Using 'postcss-sorting' plugin synchronously for sorting CSS declarations.
pros: Plugin is synchronous and easy to configure.
Works well with ESLint fix feature.
No need for hacky workarounds.
cons: May separate linked CSS properties due to alphabetical sorting.
Requires configuration and integration effort.

template_adherence.title: ADR 0013: Replace GitLab CI + Clever app with simple object storage hosting for previews
template_adherence.context: We used to have a GitLab CI integration to publish previews of the Storybook for any given branch. template_adherence.decision_drivers: The main drivers were reducing the time to get live previews from 7-8 minutes to under 1 minute, simplifying the deployment process, and enabling faster iteration for developers. template_adherence.decision: The decision was to replace the GitLab CI + Clever Node.js app system with a simpler approach: build locally on the developer's machine and publish the static files to Cellar, Clever Cloud's S3 compatible object storage. template_adherence.consequences: Positive consequences include much faster preview deployment (under 1 minute), simpler process relying on developer machines, and added flexibility with helper scripts. Negative consequences include lack of good HTTP compression and cache settings, and the current implementation being a work in progress with room for improvement.

template_adherence.title: Introducing a custom WDS plugin based on esbuild
template_adherence.context: The ADR describes the context of using a prebuilt version of Storybook based on Web Dev Server (WDS) that improves performance by avoiding the default Webpack setup. It explains the introduction of several ES module dependencies (RxJS, Leaflet, chart.js) and the impact on loading times due to many files being loaded individually by the browser.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include the need to improve Storybook's local development load times, the increase in HTTP requests due to ES module dependencies, and uncertainty about future Storybook improvements. Desired qualities include faster load times and reduced HTTP requests.
template_adherence.decision: The decision was to create a custom Web Dev Server plugin using esbuild to bundle some dependencies on the fly, reducing the number of HTTP requests and improving load times significantly.
template_adherence.consequences: The consequence is a reduction in HTTP requests from over 620 to less than 320 and load times reduced from 38s to 24s (cold) and 12s to 7s (cached). It also leaves open the possibility to contribute the plugin to the Modern Web project and to revisit the solution when Storybook improvements arrive.

alternatives.description: Wait for official Storybook improvements (possibly based on Vite) to improve performance.
pros: No need to maintain custom plugin code.
Benefit from official, possibly better integrated solutions.
cons: Uncertain timeline for improvements.
Current performance issues remain unresolved in the meantime.

alternatives.description: Continue using the prebuilt Storybook without bundling, accepting slower load times.
pros: No additional development effort.
Simplicity and stability of current setup.
cons: Longer load times impacting developer experience.
High number of HTTP requests.

template_adherence.title: Embracing Custom Elements Manifest
template_adherence.context: The ADR discusses the transition from using Web Component Analyzer (WCA) to adopting the new Custom Elements Manifest (CEM) standard and its analyzer tool for documenting Web Components. It outlines the limitations of the previous approach, including customization difficulties and performance issues, and presents the new CEM format and analyzer as a solution.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: Need for better customization of component documentation, improved performance in generating documentation, compatibility with Storybook, and alignment with emerging standards for Web Components documentation.
template_adherence.decision: Adopt the Custom Elements Manifest (CEM) standard and use the CEM analyzer tool with custom plugins to generate documentation. Integrate the generated manifest with Storybook via a transformer to maintain compatibility while benefiting from improved performance and customization.
template_adherence.consequences: Improved documentation customization and performance, ability to run documentation generation in watch mode, removal of dependency on WCA, and alignment with a community-driven standard. Some manual integration work is required until Storybook fully supports CEM format.

alternatives.description: Continue using Web Component Analyzer (WCA) with its JSON output and Storybook's docs addon.
pros: Existing setup is already in place and working.
No immediate need to change tooling.
cons: Limited customization capabilities.
Slower performance (8 seconds generation time).
Manual addition of custom information is error prone.

alternatives.description: Use WCA's Markdown output with Storybook's notes addon.
pros: Simple integration with Storybook notes addon.
Markdown is human-readable.
cons: Less structured and machine-readable than JSON.
Limited customization.
Deprecated in favor of JSON output.

alternatives.description: Wait for Storybook to natively support CEM format before adopting it.

template_adherence.decision: The decision is to author a Service Documentation page in Mana for each Web SRE Service, using a specific template and structure, with defined audiences and content scope. template_adherence.title: 3. Use EKS Cluster as Default Container Platform
template_adherence.context: There are quite a few options when choosing a platform and infrastructure patterns for managing applications. Across Mozilla teams, services & applications are already overwhelmingly containerized using Docker. We can deploy these containerized applications onto a number of options, including but not limited to multiple Kubernetes services or self-hosted routes.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: Not explicitly stated as a separate section, but implied drivers include the need to standardize container platform infrastructure, reduce complexity, improve security posture, and ease of access management.
template_adherence.decision: We will support Dockerized applications primarily, with some flexibility given to application components that greatly benefit from serverless architectures. Dockerized applications are deployed to Kubernetes, defaulting to a Web SRE shared applications clusters if not requiring their own Kubernetes cluster. We will use AWS' Elastic Kubernetes Service to manage our Kubernetes clusters, unless there is a documented reason for a particular project not to. We will deploy our EKS clusters using Terraform & our internal Terraform module, unless there is a documented reason for a particular project not to. Any divergences from the above decisions must be clearly documented in the project's or application's service documentation.
template_adherence.consequences: Reduces complexity of setting up our own infrastructure, or context switching between multiple container platform infrastructures. Incurs EKS costs. Will require migrations from old setups (Kops, External-terraform EKS module). EKS access model should improve our security posture and ease of access. Users must have SSO access to get to a cluster, so employees exiting limits access more reliably than previous k8s models. Having the correct AWS permissions allows you to create the k8s credentials needed to interact with the cluster, so we no longer have to pass a secret file around between people.

template_adherence.title: 4. Use 1 Kubernetes Cluster Per Environment
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include the need to support multiple environments with different purposes and uptime requirements, the desire to have clear boundaries between environments, the need to support staging environments especially for infrastructure changes, and considerations about operational support and deployment pipelines. Also, minimizing divergence between stage and production clusters and managing availability expectations for different environments are key concerns.
template_adherence.decision: For Web SRE Services environments - dev, stage, prod - that are Kubernetes-based, the decision is to use a distinct Kubernetes cluster per environment within the same infrastructure account. Additionally, use a distinct Kubernetes namespace within each cluster per application. Applications and operational changes are deployed to the appropriate clusters according to environment. Development clusters have lower availability expectations and may have automatic updates; stage and prod clusters have higher availability and stricter release policies. The stage cluster is used to validate infrastructure and application code before production deployment. Some exclusions and caveats are noted, such as not mandating immediate migration of existing services and leaving some implementation details to SRE discretion.
template_adherence.consequences: Positive consequences include having a clear pattern supporting separate staging environments and clearer boundaries between environments. Negative consequences include the work required to migrate existing services, and the inconvenience for users having to switch between clusters to compare environment states, though tooling mitigates this somewhat.

alternatives.description: Use one namespace per environment in a shared Kubernetes cluster.
pros: Simplifies cluster management by having a single cluster.
Reduces infrastructure overhead compared to multiple clusters.
cons: Less isolation between environments, which can lead to interference.
Harder to enforce strict boundaries and uptime requirements per environment.

alternatives.description: Use distinct node pool(s) per environment within a single cluster along with selectors, taints, and tolerations.
pros: Provides some level of environment separation within a single cluster.
Can optimize resource usage by sharing cluster infrastructure.
cons: Complex to manage and configure correctly.
Potential for environment interference and harder to guarantee isolation.

template_adherence.title: 5. web-sre-kubernetes-secrets-pattern
template_adherence.context:
Secrets are inconsistently managed across our various clusters. This makes it hard to trace where secrets come from and update them. It also increases our exposure to security issues, as our each tool used can become compromised independently. Current known secret management includes git-crypt repos, with sops, that apply kubernetes secrets direct to the cluster; sealed secrets; and external secrets pointing at cloud provider secret storage.

There are a few other methods that treat things that should be secrets incorrectly. For example, baking the 'secrets' into the docker image directly. This is a bad state to be in, and we will treat those situations with more urgency, correcting the pattern as soon as possible after this ADR is accepted.

The goal of this document is to describe the happy path for passing secrets to kubernetes based applications. In general non-kubernetes secrets management is out of scope for this document, but we will cover how serverless deployments (lambdas) and CI/CD are impacted by this choice, and what we expect those to look like after adopting the ADR.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include the need for a consistent, secure, and traceable secret management approach across clusters; reducing security exposure by limiting secret management methods; ease of use and maintenance for operators; alignment with best practices such as the 12 Factor App pattern; and minimizing complexity by choosing a single secret storage and retrieval method.
template_adherence.decision: The decision is to store secrets in the cloud provider secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager), then use external secrets (https://github.com/external-secrets/kubernetes-external-secrets) to retrieve those secrets and present them to pods as environment variables. This approach leverages the security and ease of use of cloud secret managers, aligns with Kubernetes best practices, and allows explicit references to secrets in source code without exposing secret values. The ADR excludes developer write access to secrets, limiting secret management to SREs/Operators with elevated privileges. The pattern for AWS Secrets Manager keys is standardized to facilitate IAM access control. Other methods such as git-crypt, sealed secrets, SSM Parameter Store, Hashicorp Vault, and embedding secrets in images or source code are explicitly not chosen due to various drawbacks.
template_adherence.consequences: Positive consequences include fewer secret management methods, simplifying rotation and updates; explicit gatekeeping of secret additions increasing control; safer referencing of secrets in CI/CD and repos without leaking values; and the ability to update secrets incrementally by pod. Negative consequences include the risk and effort involved in migrating secrets to this solution; increased unplanned work for the SRE/Operator team; potential long recovery time if the secrets manager is lost; manual steps required to update secrets and pods; and possible duplication of secrets between application and pipeline secrets.

alternatives.description: Continue using git-crypt secret repos with sops to Kubernetes secrets directly.
pros: Existing method already in use.
Allows storing secrets in git repositories.
cons: Many manual steps to get secrets to production.
Difficult to remove access after people leave (git-crypt doesn't support removing keys, requiring re-encryption).
Increases risk of secret leakage.
Inconsistent with the chosen standard.

alternatives.description: Use sealed secrets.
pros: Workflow and pattern similar to external secrets.
Allows encrypting secrets for Kubernetes.
cons: Maintaining both sealed secrets and external secrets doubles maintenance burden with little extra benefit.
Requires extra CLI tools and setup on operator computers, making it slightly more difficult to use than external secrets.

alternatives.description: Use SSM Parameter Store for secrets (used by lambdas/codebuilds).
pros: Already used by some services like lambdas and codebuilds.
Earlier version of secrets manager.
cons: Splitting secrets between two places leads to duplication.
Maintaining both workflows is sub-optimal.

alternatives.description: Build new systems like Hashicorp Vault.
pros: Potentially more control and features.
cons: Entire project in itself, requiring significant effort.
'Buy' choice (cloud secret managers) is good enough, so not chosen.

alternatives.description: Add secrets directly to docker images or source code.
pros: Easy to implement initially.
cons: Explicitly a bad practice as informed by security.
Makes it very easy to leak secrets to the world.
High priority to fix these situations.

template_adherence.title: Use cache instead of wb_terms for efficient fetching of data needed to display an entity in the short form
template_adherence.context:
When an item or a property is displayed in the short form, either as a link, or as a simple text reference, data needed to render this short form are currently loaded from the SQL table (wb_terms). wb_terms is causing several significant issues, and is not possible to be maintained any more in the long run.

Decision to use wb_terms, initially introduced as a SQL search index, has been tracked down to change 176650. As discussed there in the code review, and also in related discussions, it seems there had been no dramatic performance improvements expected, neither noticed after switching to use wb_terms instead of loading the data of the entire item or property.

Wikibase already uses MediaWiki's caching mechanisms (in production Wikidata environment being based on memcached) to reduce loading of full entity data.

In case of lexemes or forms, entity types provided by WikibaseLexeme extension, that have different internal structure than items and properties, wb_terms has not been used as a source of data for short form display. Full lexeme data has been loaded instead. Early tests didn't show significant performance issues. Also, due to different internal structure of lexemes or forms, and the way how their "short form" displayed is built, the possible use of wb_terms has not even seem feasible without changing the semantics of the table.
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
- Need to improve or maintain efficient fetching of data for short form display.
- Existing wb_terms SQL table causes significant issues and is not maintainable long term.
- No significant performance gains observed from using wb_terms.
- Existing caching mechanisms (memcached) are already in use.
- Different entity types (lexemes/forms) have different data structures.
- Potential performance impact and cache invalidation considerations.
template_adherence.decision:
Stop using wb_terms as a data source for short form display since it does not bring significant performance gains.

Retrieve data of the whole entity from storage layer (database or cached storage already in place).

If not efficient enough, store data needed for display in cache (e.g., label of an item in a particular language) to reduce computation, especially for language fallback.

This approach balances maintainability and performance.
template_adherence.consequences:
- Possible that the new way of displaying entities performs worse due to lack of reliable benchmarks.
- Switching back to wb_terms solution is a quick fix if serious problems arise.
- Increased use of memcached might impact caching system performance due to more entries.
- Cache invalidation mechanisms need consideration and are left for a more specific ADR.
- The wb_terms table has been removed in 2020.

alternatives.description: Continue using wb_terms as the data source for short form display.
pros: Familiar approach with existing implementation.
Potentially no immediate changes required.
cons: wb_terms causes significant issues and is not maintainable long term.
No significant performance improvements observed.
Does not leverage existing caching mechanisms effectively.

alternatives.description: Load full entity data every time without caching or using wb_terms.
pros: Simplifies data retrieval logic.
Avoids reliance on problematic wb_terms table.
cons: Potentially higher performance cost due to loading full data.
May not scale well for large instances like Wikidata.

alternatives.description: Use caching mechanisms to store only necessary data for short form display.
pros: Reduces computation needed for display, especially with language fallback.
Leverages existing caching infrastructure (memcached).
Improves maintainability by avoiding wb_terms.
cons: Requires cache invalidation mechanisms.
Increased load on caching system.
Needs careful design to ensure performance gains.

template_adherence.title: Use PSR-16 PHP Cache Interface in Wikibase
template_adherence.context:
Wikibase uses cache in different parts of PHP code base. Wikibase itself does not provide any abstraction for cache implementation. Instead MediaWiki-specific classes, such as abstract `BagOStuff`, or `WANObjectCache`, are used in code.

The [PSR-16] standard defines an abstract Simple Cache interface for use in PHP code.

More formal and verbose Caching interface has been defined as [PSR-6].
We find it overly verbose compared to simpler [PSR-16], which we favour here.

Possible use of [PSR-16] in MediaWiki is out of scope of this decision.
It might be a possible next step.
In this regard it is possibly worth mentioning that using [PSR-6] interface in MediaWiki has been proposed in 2016, but it has been declined (see: [T130528]).
It should also be noted that there is already a PSR-6 adapter for the `BagOStuff`: https://packagist.org/packages/addshore/psr-6-mediawiki-bagostuff-adapter.
There are already adapters that can use a PSR-16 cache as a PSR-6 cache and vice versa: https://symfony.com/doc/current/components/cache/psr6_psr16_adapters.html.
Also, as `Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface` and `Psr\SimpleCache\CacheInterface` declare only one method of the same name, `clear()`, and as both declarations have the same signature, any cache system may implement both interfaces.
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
- Need for a simple, standard cache interface in Wikibase PHP code.
- Avoiding direct dependency on MediaWiki-specific cache classes.
- Preference for PSR-16 over PSR-6 due to simplicity.
- Desire to enable easier testing and mocking.
- Potential future flexibility to switch cache implementations.
- Existing adapters and compatibility between PSR-16 and PSR-6.
- Avoiding adding unnecessary verbosity or complexity.
template_adherence.decision:
We will introduce PSR-16-compliant cache interface to Wikibase.
New PHP code using cache will use this abstraction, instead of binding directly to MediaWiki cache classes, or any other specific third-party implementations.

We will use [psr/simple-cache] library to add `CacheInterface` to Wikibase.
template_adherence.consequences:
[psr/simple-cache] library will be added as a PHP dependency to Wikibase.
This also means adding the library to `mediawiki-vendor` component of WMF.

PHP code will be hinting against the abstract [PSR-16] `CacheInterface`.
Existing MediaWiki's `BagOStuff` cache services could still be used.
Some [PSR-16]-compliant implementation, or implementations, wrapping over `BagOStuff`, or `WANObjectCache`, will be added.

It will be possible to create code in Wikibase that uses cache, without needing to add dependency to MediaWiki.

It will be easy to replace real cache implementations with test doubles in Wikibase test code.
In particular, there will be no need for tests to depend on MediaWiki only to be able to mock `BagOStuff` class.

Potential switching parts of Wikibase code to use different (e.g. non-MediaWiki's) cache implementation is going to be possible as long as there is PSR-16-compliant interface to the cache.

alternatives.description: Continue using MediaWiki-specific cache classes like `BagOStuff` and `WANObjectCache` directly without introducing PSR-16 interface.
pros: No additional dependencies added.
No changes to existing codebase required.
cons: Tight coupling to MediaWiki cache implementations.
Harder to test and mock cache usage.
Less flexibility to switch cache implementations in future.

alternatives.description: Adopt PSR-6 caching interface instead of PSR-16.
pros: More formal and feature-rich caching interface.
Standardized and widely used in some PHP projects.
cons: Overly verbose compared to PSR-16.
Previously proposed and declined for MediaWiki.
Adds complexity that may not be needed.

template_adherence.title: 2) CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore caching method
template_adherence.context:
The [PropertyInfoStore] interfaces with the [wb_property_info] DB table holding information about wikibase properties.
The [CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore] stores the whole of the [wb_property_info]  table in a single cache key.
The Wikibase wiring is setup to provide this CacheAware store using the default cache (memcached for WMF).

The [CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore] has a high number of reads, and the method of storing the whole table in a single key
results in lots of traffic to a single memcached instance as described in [T97368].
The amount of traffic for the memcached key has steadily grown as the number of properties in the store have grown.
This traffic also moves between memcached servers after each WMF deploy as the cache key changes.
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
High read volume on CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore causing heavy traffic to a single memcached instance.
Traffic increasing with number of properties.
Need to reduce memcached traffic without major code rework.
Desire for a trivial code change solution.
Avoid complexity in cache purging by using short TTL.
template_adherence.decision:
A layer of APC caching (per server) is added on top of the shared memcached caching.
This is done in the service wiring by wrapping our [CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore] in another [CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore].
This on APC cache has a short TTL to avoid the need to actively think about purging.
Adding this extra layer of caching was chosen rather than anything more drastic as it is a trivial code change vs re-working how the [CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore] works.
template_adherence.consequences:
Requests could end up with a slightly out of date [PropertyInfoStore] after a new property is created or updated, but this would soon be fixed by the short TTL.

The ever increasing traffic for the individual memcached server has decreased.
https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T97368#4741600

We will need to work again on this area and either:
- Split the cache up per property
- More requests to memcached, but less overall data retrieved
- Much better distribution of keys between servers
- Introduce more than 1 cache key for the same data to spread the traffic load
- These cache keys could still end up on the same server
- Duplicating this data more is evil
- Increase the TTL for the on web server caching
- This will slowly lead to increased time before all servers are in sync.

alternatives.description: Re-working how the CacheAwarePropertyInfoStore works to reduce memcached traffic.
pros: Potentially more efficient caching strategy.
Could reduce traffic more significantly.
cons: Requires more complex code changes.
Higher development effort.
Longer implementation time.

alternatives.description: Splitting the cache up per property.
pros: More granular caching.
Better distribution of keys between servers.
cons: More requests to memcached.
Potentially more complex cache management.
Risk of duplicating data.

alternatives.description: Increasing the TTL for the on web server caching.
pros: Reduces frequency of cache refreshes.
Less traffic to memcached.
cons: Longer time before all servers are in sync.
Potentially stale data for longer periods.

template_adherence.title: 3) Termbox ParserCache Integration
template_adherence.context: The new Termbox (v2) introduces an external SSR service to Wikibase that generates server-side markup for user-specific content on Item and Property pages. User-specific configuration depends on parameters like preferred languages and toggle states, which affect caching strategies. The existing ParserCache accounts for some parameters but not all user-specific ones. The previous Termbox (v1) workaround is not viable for Termbox (v2). ParserCache significantly reduces render time and is heavily used, with a notable portion of requests from logged-in users requiring customized results.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The need to efficiently cache non-user-specific content while handling user-specific variations, the performance impact of caching strategies, the architectural constraints of Termbox (v2), and the frequency and nature of user requests influencing cache hit rates.
template_adherence.decision: Cache the non-user-specific version of Termbox (v2) as part of ParserOutput. Serve cached results for users with default configurations. For users with different configurations, make a later request to the Termbox (v2) service during the request lifecycle and serve its result. If the SSR service fails, serve an empty element to be replaced by client-side rendering. More complex fallbacks are deferred to product management.
template_adherence.consequences: ParserOutput remains free of user-specific markup, avoiding further cache splitting. Users with custom configurations may experience slower render times due to uncached SSR service requests. The SSR service must be performant. Logging will monitor default configuration usage to maximize cache hits and minimize SSR requests.

alternatives.description: Use the PlaceholderEmittingEntityTermsView approach from Termbox (v1) to inject markers and replace user-specific markup before rendering.
pros: Allows caching of non-user-specific content separately.
Avoids uncached SSR requests for user-specific content.
cons: Not viable for Termbox (v2) due to architectural differences.
Splits logic across two services, complicating maintenance.

template_adherence.title: 4) Make ChangeOp::apply() return ChangeOpResult
template_adherence.context: `wbeditentity` summary message for Wikibase Items and Properties provides very little information on what have been changed on the entity, with the main message in the summary being "Item Changed". In [T220696], we want to update those summary messages generated for Wikibase Items and Properties when using `wbeditentity` to be more detailed and informative. Wikibase Lexeme achieved generating detailed summary messages by: 1. making its  implementations update the summary object passed to the change op instance with granular information about the change. 2. implementing [SummaryAggregator] class and using it internally in some [ChangeOp] implementations (some of those that are non-leaf nodes and contain further change ops) in order to combine those summary messages generated by leaf nodes (the effective change ops in the tree).
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include: the need for more detailed and informative summary messages for Wikibase Items and Properties; the desire for a clean design that separates concerns; the existing design where ChangeOp handles multiple responsibilities including summary message generation; the potential benefits of using a standard pattern (Visitor Pattern) for tree structures; the need to avoid breaking changes for WikibaseLexeme; and the cost of initial implementation and refactoring.
template_adherence.decision: The decision is to adopt the visitor pattern design. Specifically, ChangeOp::apply() will be changed to return a ChangeOpResult interface encapsulating the result of applying a change op to an entity document. This allows extracting summary message generation out of ChangeOp, simplifying its design and scoping down its domain and dependencies. The decision includes next steps to implement ChangeOpResult and update ChangeOp implementations accordingly.
template_adherence.consequences: The main consequence is that Wikibase and WikibaseLexeme will have two separate ways to achieve similar requirements, causing short-term inconsistency of design. This should be mitigated by a follow-up refactoring task to unify the design. Additionally, changing ChangeOp interface will cause CI failures due to circular dependencies, requiring a staged update approach. There is also a hint that ChangeOp concepts might be better moved into a separate library for proper versioning and dependency management.

alternatives.description: Reusing current pattern where ChangeOp implementations update the summary object passed to them and use SummaryAggregator internally.
pros: Leverages existing design and implementation.
No major refactoring needed.
cons: Feels off with regards to clean design.
ChangeOp handles multiple concerns, mixing applying changes and summary generation.
Does not use standard design patterns for tree structures.

alternatives.description: Visitor pattern design where a visitor operates over the change ops hierarchy to generate summaries, and ChangeOp::apply() returns ChangeOpResult.
pros: Uses a more standard pattern with tree structures.
Extracts summary message generation out of ChangeOp, simplifying its design.
Scopes down domain and dependencies of ChangeOp.
Avoids breaking changes for WikibaseLexeme.
cons: Requires initial implementation and refactoring.
Introduces short-term inconsistency between Wikibase and WikibaseLexeme.
Causes CI issues due to interface changes requiring staged updates.

template_adherence.title: Invalidate ParserCache on backwards incompatible frontend changes
template_adherence.context:
When changes to the markup used on entity pages are made we often end up with outdated content in the ParserCache. This can result in user facing errors from either the backend code attempting to perform processing on ParserCache output or frontend Javascript attempting to access parts of the DOM that have changed.

Examples of this are:
* [T228978] - Backend attempting to fill placeholders that it doesn't expect to be there.
* [T205330] - Frontend looking for a newly introduced data-attribute that isn't present in historic parser cache entries.

In the not distant past we have solved these problems by introducing a custom [RejectParserCacheValue Hook] in operations/mediawiki-config e.g. (https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/c/operations/mediawiki-config/+/463221) to reject cache entries made before deployment time.

We've also done it in stages leaving some invalid entries in the cache to avoid increased load from marking all entries as invalid at once.

While this has worked for us in the past we have typically applied it after discovering a problem. Even then the way we gradually reject historic invalid cached results in user facing errors for some time.
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
The need to avoid user facing errors caused by outdated ParserCache content due to frontend markup changes.
The desire to handle backwards incompatible changes gracefully without causing widespread cache invalidation spikes.
The ability to support gradual rollout, A/B testing, and reversion of features.
The existing mechanisms like RejectParserCacheValue Hook and ParserOptions that can be leveraged.
The concern about increased cache size and server load if all cache entries are invalidated at once.
template_adherence.decision:
We should record things that impact the ParserOutput content (e.g. the version of the code used to generate the ParserOutput) in the parser options. These parser options should then be marked as used in generating the ParserCache key. The RejectParserCacheValue can be used if the two versions of the ParserOutput content cannot coexist and backwards compatibility is not possible.

In this way we will split the ParserCache into old and new versions. An example of this was trialled when introducing new mobile Termbox. See: https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/c/mediawiki/extensions/Wikibase/+/529055.

In the event that we are tracking a new part of the code that doesn't currently have a corresponding option then it may be necessary to ensure it is introduced. The ParserOptions used to calculate the ParserCache key are determined from existing cache entries. Thus on introducing a new key (but not a new key value) a custom RejectParserCacheValue Hook may still be required. See: https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/c/mediawiki/extensions/Wikibase/+/529059 for an example.

An option already exists (but hasn't been used in the last 4 years) on [EntityContent] ([EntityHandler::PARSER_VERSION]) which may be useful for some changes. However, currently this applies to all entities; in general we usually only make changes to one type of entity at a time so more options will be needed.
template_adherence.consequences:
If this is followed we should avoid user facing errors when making breaking frontend changes.

We are able to serve without additional hacks both the current and old versions of the ParserCache output. This means we can:
* A/B test the feature
* gradually roll out the feature across entities
* revert a broken feature

However, if the feature is suddenly turned on for all users on all entities then we may see a spike in ParserCache size and application server load as we initially always miss the cache. Therefore "big bang" breaking changes should be done with caution, and gradual rollouts should be preferred.

template_adherence.title: 6) Use Package Modules for dependency management within ResourceLoader modules
template_adherence.context:
Until recently, frontend dependencies in Wikibase were managed through globally registered ResourceLoader modules with no distinction between internal dependencies and modules that needed to be publicly available. This resulted in more than 250 ResourceLoader modules with a very complex dependency relationship. The names of all modules are loaded with every page view, affecting page load time and network overhead. See T228513

We considered two options to reduce the number of globally registered ResourceLoader modules: webpack and ResourceLoader Package Modules.

Solving the problem with webpack would have involved the introduction of a build step to create bundles for each of the top-level (=entry point) modules. Advantages of this approach are superior minification at build time - better than the ResourceLoader minification, and all the other benefits of introducing a build step such as transpilation from more modern ES versions, and easier reuse of 3rd party npm libraries. The risks we identified for this approach include;

- Having to generate and check in the bundled js files in addition to their source. That would lead to most patches having a merge conflict.
- Having to rewrite tests for internal files that can no longer run within the QUnit ResourceLoader test suite.
- Webpack is not yet widely adopted within the MediaWiki ecosystem.
- Putting in too much work into (legacy) parts of the code that are not going to change any time soon.

For Package Modules, we agreed that we would be missing out many of the positive side effects of introducing webpack and the build step. On the other hand, this solution would require fewer code changes, and would be the recommended MediaWiki way to solve the problem at hand.
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
- Need to reduce the number of globally registered ResourceLoader modules to improve page load time and reduce network overhead.
- Desire to avoid complex dependency relationships and large startup manifests.
- Consideration of ease of migration and testing.
- Risk assessment of introducing a build step with webpack.
- Compatibility with existing testing frameworks and ecosystem adoption.
- Future flexibility to switch approaches if needed.
template_adherence.decision:
We decided to go with Package Modules instead of webpack and reduced the number of modules that Wikibase registers from 260 to 85.

The reasons for choosing Package Modules include:
- Easier migration for a large codebase.
- Easier adaptation of tests given the current paradigm of running QUnit tests in ResourceLoader and browser context.
- Future possibility to switch to webpack remains feasible since both understand require.
- Avoidance of rebase conflicts that would arise from checking in bundled files into version control.

Webpack is still used in submodules that work independently of Wikibase to run tests in the context of karma + webpack + node, while ResourceLoader understands those notations when the code is pulled as a ResourceLoader module in the Wikibase extension.
template_adherence.consequences:
- Reduced the size of the startup manifest in the Startup Module, which is loaded on every page view, thereby reducing overall traffic.
- Development and debugging are easier due to the use of require() to load dependencies.
- Statistical impact is documented in T232492.

Overall, the decision improved performance and maintainability while balancing migration effort and ecosystem compatibility.

template_adherence.title: 7) Use vuex-smart-modules in Data Bridge
template_adherence.context:
The Wikidata Bridge app uses VueJs version 2 and Vuex version 3 for state management.
Both within the store and in vue components the calls to `dispatch()` and `commit()` are not type safe.
That means that they accept any arguments and TypeScript will still compile without error.
Since `dispatch()` and `commit()` are typical seams that are usually mocked during unit testing,
it is up to integration, end-to-end and browser tests to detect these errors.

This is particularly unfortunate as the store is one of the central locations where business logic happens.

We considered two options:
1. writing our own set of wrappers for `dispatch()` and `commit()` to get type safety
1. using vuex-smart-modules

The advantages of doing it ourselves included us not having another dependency.
The risks include that this would be yet another homebrew layer of abstraction.

The advantages of using vuex-smart-modules include:
- it gives us proper native type safety both in the store and in components
- we can call actions/getters/mutations with [method style access](https://github.com/ktsn/vuex-smart-module#method-style-access-for-actions-and-mutations)
- we can get rid of all the `BRIDGE_SET_TARGET_VALUE` constants without having to fall back to string literals
- we can actually use the IDE's `go to method definition` functionality
- we can rely on the action's return type instead of dispatch's `Promise<any>` being used everywhere
- we can drop the `vuex-class` dependency as we can use vuex-smart-modules for all store access in components
- it is developed by a VueJs core contributor

The risks include:
- it is still a very new project with a 0.x.y version number
- it is another layer on top of vuex, which means the documentation may not be as good as it could be
- we are the first big project to use it
- mocking of dependencies and nested modules in testing still seems to be not handled as diligently as one would wish
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The drivers include the need for type safety in Vuex store dispatch and commit calls, reducing errors caught only in integration or end-to-end tests, improving developer experience with IDE features, and balancing risks of adding a new dependency versus maintaining homegrown solutions.
template_adherence.decision: We decided to rewrite our Vuex store using vuex-smart-modules version 0.3.4
template_adherence.consequences: Expected consequences include improved type safety in dispatch and commit calls, ability to use method style access, and better IDE support. Negative consequences include limitations in dependency injection, testing challenges, module nesting depth limits, and being early adopters of a new library. Future learnings are to be added as experience grows.

alternatives.description: Writing our own set of wrappers for `dispatch()` and `commit()` to get type safety.
pros: No additional dependencies.
cons: Would be another homebrew layer of abstraction.

alternatives.description: Using vuex-smart-modules.
pros: Provides proper native type safety in store and components.
Enables method style access for actions and mutations.
Removes need for string literal constants.
Improves IDE navigation to method definitions.
Allows relying on action return types instead of generic Promise<any>.
Drops dependency on vuex-class.
Developed by a VueJs core contributor.
cons: New project with 0.x.y version number.
Additional layer on top of Vuex with potentially less documentation.
First big project to use it, so unknowns remain.
Testing mocking of dependencies and nested modules not fully mature.

template_adherence.title: 8) Format Bridge references via API
template_adherence.context: Data Bridge is a browser-side application that allows users to edit Wikidata from Wikibase Client wikis. This involves showing users references for the statements they are editing, in a readable format. The guiding example for this format is the following reference from the South Pole Telescope article, which is generated by Lua code from the Wikidata reference. The reference involves formatting multiple datatypes not initially supported by Data Bridge. Other extensions may add more datatypes, making browser-side formatting unattractive. Server-side code already knows how to format every datatype for presentation. Wikibase has an API for formatting individual values but it is limited to single values, requiring many API requests for rich references. Some values should be combined, such as URL and title into a link. Future Data Bridge support for editing references requires displaying unsaved references.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The need to format complex references involving multiple datatypes, the limitations of client-side formatting, the existing server-side formatting capabilities, the inefficiency of multiple API calls for individual values, the need to combine certain values into a single formatted output, and future support for editing references that may not yet be saved.
template_adherence.decision: To add an action API module to Wikibase Client that accepts a reference JSON blob and returns HTML. This module encodes knowledge such as combining certain values and property order. The functionality will be useful for other API users and as a Lua function for wiki content, initially marked internal for Data Bridge. The action API is chosen as the most straightforward option, and Wikibase Client is chosen because the desired formatting aligns more closely with the client.
template_adherence.consequences: A wbformatreference API module will be added to Wikibase Client with parameters for the reference JSON, style (initially only internal-data-bridge), and output format (initially only html). Property IDs for key reference properties will be configurable. The formatting functionality will be encapsulated in a PHP service returning wikitext parsed into HTML. Reference snaks are emitted in a specific order with translatable separators. URL and title are combined into a single link if both present. Labels are shown in user language without links. The approach contrasts with recent Wikibase Repository direction favoring TypeScript/JavaScript and server-side rendering, but aligns with Wikibase Client's PHP-based rendering needs. template_adherence.title: 9) Refactor hooks for testability
template_adherence.context:
Currently, the `RepoHooks` class remains largely untested due to a combination of two factors:

1. The methods in this class are static, and we do not own the contract under which they should be called, as they are
defined as hooks in `extension.json` or as global variables in the entrypoints e.g. [extensions/Wikibase/repo/Wikibase.php:1020](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki-extensions-Wikibase/blob/7b20d22b3c0bbc37ad23f63e38fadc9b1f2ca057/repo/Wikibase.php#L1020), which means we cannot easily refactor the methods to increase testability

2. Methods rely heavily on the `WikibaseRepo` singleton and it's store, which make it harder to test, as there is no
way to to inject a mock of `WikibaseRepo` without dependency injection.

A [RFC for enabling dependency injection](https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T240307) in hooks is currently under way.
However, an interim solution is needed in order to mitigate the amount of untested logic that exists in that file
and other places in the codebase.

While reviewing this issue, two initial solutions were considered:

- Refactor `RepoHooks` into a singleton itself, so that when instantiated, we can inject a Mock of `WikibaseRepo`
instead of using the real deal.
- Adopt a pattern used in `WikibaseClient` Which enables us to mock several parts of it (namely the store), and replace
the real store by creating an `overrideStore` method. See in following:
- [`client/tests/phpunit/includes/MockClientStore.php`](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki-extensions-Wikibase/blob/master/client/tests/phpunit/includes/MockClientStore.php)
- [`client/tests/phpunit/includes/DataAccess/ParserFunctions/PropertyParserFunctionIntegrationTest.php:42`](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki-extensions-Wikibase/blob/master/client/tests/phpunit/includes/DataAccess/ParserFunctions/PropertyParserFunctionIntegrationTest.php#L42)

However, after a discussion, it was decided to implement a middle ground, that would enable us to gradually refactor
hooks, rather than a one time big change.
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
- Need to increase testability of the `RepoHooks` class.
- Current static methods and reliance on singleton make testing difficult.
- Desire to enable dependency injection for better mocking.
- Interim solution needed before full dependency injection is implemented.
- Desire to have a pattern that allows gradual refactoring rather than a big one-time change.
- Consistency with existing patterns in the codebase.
- Improve test coverage and maintainability.
template_adherence.decision:
It was decided to adopt an existing pattern in Wikibase repo where each hook handler gets its own singleton class and
provides at least four methods:

- A constructor to make dependency injection easier.
- A public static method to bootstrap an instance from global settings. For consistency, this would typically be named
`newFromGlobalSettings`.
- (optional) A public static method to get a cached instance of the handler object (rather than instantiate it each time):
This is useful for hooks handlers which are called several times.
- A public static method to wire up functionality into the hooks system and should contain little to no logic (as it is
hard to test without complete integration or e2e tests).
- A public method to perform the actual handler logic in a testable way.

This class should be placed under the `includes/Hooks` directory. An example of this pattern can be seen in:
https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/c/mediawiki/extensions/Wikibase/+/574495
template_adherence.consequences:
- Increase in the ability to test code for hooks, as well as general test coverage.

- Deciding on a single source of truth regarding hooks will encourage common understanding and help newcomers to the
code refactor and write their own hooks.

- Decoupling the tests from the actual store might make tests run faster, as no connections to the Database / reads or
writes will be made.

- Adopting a pattern regarding testing hooks, can help guide us in refactoring and writing new
pieces of code which are considered "hard to test".

- This doesn't provide a pattern for end-to-end testing of hooks, i.e. running of the public static method for hook
wiring isn't covered by this pattern.

alternatives.description: Refactor `RepoHooks` into a singleton itself, so that when instantiated, we can inject a Mock of `WikibaseRepo` instead of using the real deal.
pros: Allows dependency injection for easier mocking.
Centralizes hook handling in a singleton.
cons: Might be a big change and not incremental.
Could be complex to implement given existing static methods and contracts.

alternatives.description: Adopt a pattern used in `WikibaseClient` which enables mocking several parts, replacing the real store by creating an `overrideStore` method.
pros: Enables mocking of store for tests.
Leverages an existing pattern in the codebase.
cons: Might not fit well with hook handling.
Could require significant refactoring.

template_adherence.title: 10) Do not add source information to Property IDs for the Federated Properties MVP
template_adherence.context:
The Federated Properties MVP introduces a [federatedPropertiesEnabled] setting which enables a Wikibase instance (local wiki) to read all Properties from a remote Wikibase (source wiki). A wiki with this setting enabled can only use federated Properties and disallows the creation or use of any local Properties. Switching from Federated Properties mode back to using local Properties or vice versa is not supported.

Federated Properties use API-based implementations of entity data access services. This ADR documents our decision regarding the dispatching mechanism for the respective services, i.e. how Wikibase determines whether to use a service for handling a local Property or a federated Property.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The decision drivers are implicitly described in the 'Considered Actions' section, focusing on the trade-offs between future-proofing the system to handle multiple sources of Properties simultaneously versus implementing a simpler, less flexible solution for the MVP. Key concerns include the complexity of implementation, future extensibility, and the assumption about the number of Property sources and the immutability of the 'federatedPropertiesEnabled' setting.
template_adherence.decision: The decision is to adopt the second option: swapping out the services depending on the 'federatedPropertiesEnabled' setting. This approach is simpler, requires less work at this stage, and delays the more complex decision of handling multiple Property sources on a single wiki. The decision is expected to be revisited and likely superseded in the future.
template_adherence.consequences: The consequence is that no source information is added to federated Properties. Property services will be overridden via specific files or factory methods. The system supports only one source of Properties at a time, determined by configuration. This simplifies the current implementation but may require revisiting as requirements evolve.

alternatives.description: Building the source information into the Property IDs via repository prefixes and changing all relevant services into dispatching services that delegate to either the local database-backed services or API-based services depending on the ID source.
pros: Likely the future-proof solution when both local and federated Properties co-exist on the same wiki.
Limits the effort of rewriting code later when supporting multiple sources.
cons: Requires dealing with conceptual problems not part of the MVP.
Extra upfront work including adding prefixes, mapping source information, and building dispatching layers.
More complex implementation at this stage.

alternatives.description: Swapping out the services depending on the 'federatedPropertiesEnabled' setting, assuming a single source for Properties and that the setting won't change during the wiki's lifespan.
pros: Requires less work at this stage.
Delays complex decisions about handling multiple Property sources.
Simpler implementation for the MVP.
cons: IDs of federated Properties remain indistinguishable from local ones.
Supports only one source at a time.
May require revisiting and rewriting in the future.

template_adherence.title: 11) declare strict_types Rollout
template_adherence.context: The first patch introducing a usage of `declare( strict_types = 1 );` has just been merged into Wikibase.git. Strict types are already used in some composer libraries. Strict typing means PHP will no longer automatically cast wrong scalar variables to the expected type, requiring correct types in method calls. Strict typing applies to calls made within the file with strict typing enabled, not to functions declared within that file. Benefits include avoiding subtle bugs, easier reasoning about code, and potential future performance optimizations. A strategy for rollout and maintenance is needed. PHP Codesniffer has a sniff to enforce strict types declaration. A code snippet is provided to estimate rollout progress.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: Need to adopt strict_types to improve code quality and maintainability, avoid subtle bugs, enable easier reasoning about code, and potentially improve performance. Need a strategy for progressive rollout and enforcement. Desire to track progress and avoid mass bulk changes to minimize risk.
template_adherence.decision: Progressively rollout and use strict_types across all PHP code as code is touched in regular work, including test classes and code without immediate benefit. New code should always use strict_types, ideally enforced in code review. Progress will be tracked using a code snippet and a phabricator ticket. Eventually, the RequireStrictTypes sniff will be enabled with exclusions as needed. Once strict_types is everywhere, this ADR will be deprecated.
template_adherence.consequences: Progressive movement toward strict types everywhere. No mass bulk changes, so implications of adding strict types will be considered per code change. This approach balances adoption with risk management.

alternatives.description: Do not adopt strict_types at all, continue with weak typing.
pros: No immediate changes required.
No risk of breaking existing code due to strict typing.
cons: Continued risk of subtle bugs due to type coercion.
Harder to reason about code types.
Missed opportunity for performance improvements.

alternatives.description: Adopt strict_types immediately everywhere with a mass bulk change.
pros: Immediate consistency across all code.
Faster realization of benefits of strict typing.
cons: High risk of breaking existing code.
Large effort required to fix all issues at once.
Potential disruption to development workflow.

template_adherence.title: 12) PSR-4 and maintenance scripts
template_adherence.context: PHP’s autoloading mechanism allows for automatic loading of classes or interfaces when first needed, following the PSR-4 standard. Wikibase migrated to fully follow PSR-4, but maintenance scripts posed a challenge because PSR-4 requires exact case matching between class and file names, which conflicted with traditional lowercase maintenance script file names. Some maintenance scripts needed to be autoloaded, while others did not.
template_adherence.decision_drivers: The need to comply with PSR-4 autoloading standards, maintain compatibility with existing maintenance scripts, minimize risk of errors (especially after a recent incident involving database table drops), and keep the autoloader efficient and manageable.
template_adherence.decision: Use PSR-4 for all regular source code files under includes/ or src/ directories. For maintenance scripts, add only the two scripts needed for DatabaseSchemaUpdater to AutoloadClasses. Scripts needed only for unit tests are loaded via require_once directly in those tests (option 4). Encourage future maintenance scripts to use PSR-4 compliant uppercase file names.
template_adherence.consequences: Completed migration of Wikibase classes to correct namespaces and PSR-4 compliance. No mechanism to load non-compliant files reduces risk of introducing errors. Anticipate removal of autoloaded maintenance scripts related to wb_terms table once old term storage is removed. Future changes may occur depending on MediaWiki maintenance task runner developments.

alternatives.description: Put all maintenance scripts in AutoloadClasses to be autoloaded.
pros: Reflects behavior of generated autoload.php files.
Ensures all maintenance scripts are autoloadable.
cons: May include unnecessary scripts, increasing autoloader size.
Not selective, potentially loading unneeded scripts.

alternatives.description: Put only necessary maintenance scripts in AutoloadClasses, determined by class name references.
pros: Reduces autoloader size by including only needed scripts.

cons: Requires analysis to determine necessary scripts.
Risk of missing needed scripts if analysis is incomplete.

alternatives.description: Like 2, but put scripts needed only for unit tests in TestAutoloadClasses.
pros: Keeps production autoloader smaller.

cons: Introduces difference between production and test environments.
Unclear if non-test classes should be in TestAutoloadClasses.

cons: Requires manual require_once in tests.

This extension has grown over time and become incoherent. When adding some code or functionality that can be shared between
Repo and Client developers see this as the obvious place to put it.

This results in the continued growth and increased lack of structure.

Alternative solutions were considered and rejected:
* Registering shared features in Client and then making Repo depend on Client
* Appears to go against the general logical flow of data
* Gives the impression of tighter coupling

* Keeping Lib as an extension and trying to keep the structure more defined
* Still leaves a place future developers may be tempted to "dump" shared logic

template_adherence.decision: We will stop registering WikibaseLib as a separate extension. These parts encompass: Autoloaded PHP code; MediaWiki Hooks; ResourceLoader Modules and i18n Messages.
template_adherence.consequences:

Future shared code should be distributed using composer packages.

We anticipated that shared i18n messages may need to remain jointly registered in both the Client and Repo `extension.json`.

Duplicate registration of the WikibaseLib hooks may be challenging. We will try to refactor in order to either:

* make joint registration possible.

template_adherence.title: Make Wikibase.git a monorepo
template_adherence.context:
Wikibase-related code is found in various places and under different degrees of isolation. Parts of the PHP code, especially early / fundamental parts like the data model and its serialization, are independent libraries in separate Git repositories, distributed via Composer. Some JavaScript code, such as the new Termbox, is also developed independently, and typically included as a Git submodule. On the other hand, much of Wikibase is included directly in the Wikibase Git repository, often as part of the monolithic “Lib” component.

Part of the goal of the Decoupling Hike (June to August 2020) has been to develop a strategy for refactoring this “Lib” component. We found that the separate libraries have obvious benefits thanks to being stand-alone, separate components, but also have downsides for development: it is inconvenient to have to develop the libraries in separate repository, and cumbersome to get the changes back into the main Wikibase Git repository. At best, a submodule pointer needs to be updated; at worst, the library needs to publish a new release, which then needs to make its way into [mediawiki/vendor][]. We investigated a “monorepo” approach in [T254920][], and propose that it offers the best of both worlds. Monorepos are also used by others, including the Symfony PHP framework ([blog post][Symfony blog post], [talk video][Symfony talk video]).
template_adherence.decision_drivers:
- Need to reduce inconvenience and cumbersomeness of developing libraries in separate repositories.
- Desire to have changes to libraries become immediately effective within Wikibase.
- Preserve benefits of stand-alone, separate components.
- Maintain history and ability to publish libraries separately.
- Align with practices used by other projects (e.g., Symfony PHP framework).
template_adherence.decision:
Wikibase.git will become a monorepo, containing not just the overall MediaWiki extension code but also the code and history of libraries that can stand on their own. Changes to those libraries become immediately effective within Wikibase, but are also published separately.

Where possible, sections of Wikibase Lib will be extracted into separate libraries. Dependencies on MediaWiki are removed (or replaced with suitable MediaWiki libraries, e.g. [wikimedia/timestamp][] instead of `wfTimestamp()`). Their source code is moved from subdirectories of `lib/includes/` and `lib/tests/phpunit/` into a subdirectory of `lib/packages/` named after the prospective Composer package name, and a `composer.json` file is added there. The [git filter-repo][] tool can then be used to extract a subset of the Wikibase Git history with only the changes relevant to the new library; this new read-only repository can be used as the VCS source of the Composer package, and is automatically updated through a GitHub action.

Formerly stand-alone libraries will be merged into the Wikibase Git repository. Their history will be preserved, and they will also be extracted into separate Git repositories again, using the [git filter-repo][]-based process outlined above. It is expected that it will be possible to produce identical Git hashes, making this migration transparent to other users of the libraries’ Git repositories – the repositories will simply no longer be the main source of truth.
template_adherence.consequences:
Code that was formerly part of Lib will become more stand-alone, less coupled to MediaWiki core and Wikibase, while still being developed in mostly the same fashion.

Libraries that were standalone will remain independent, but development for them will take place in the Wikibase Git repository. Changes to them will become effective immediately, without having to wait for the next release and [mediawiki/vendor][] update. “Tree-wide” changes, such as code style updates, will be easier to apply.

For new components, the source code strategy will be clear: they are expected to be developed in Wikibase, but with a setup that also extracts them as a separate Git repository (using [git filter-repo][]) right from the beginning. This removes a source of uncertainty for new projects.

Publishing these packages as separate repositories to GitHub is done for benefits such as being able to see their isolated history and contributors, and being able to run their tests in CI in isolation without surrounding Wikibase code being present.

alternatives.description: Continue developing libraries in separate repositories and use submodules or releases to integrate changes.
pros: Maintains clear separation of libraries.
Libraries can be versioned and released independently.
cons: Inconvenient to develop across multiple repositories.
Cumbersome to update submodule pointers or wait for new releases.
Slower integration of changes into main Wikibase repository.

alternatives.description: Use a fully monolithic repository without extracting libraries separately.
pros: Simplifies repository management.
All code in one place.
cons: Loses benefits of stand-alone libraries.
Harder to publish and maintain separate packages.
Potentially more coupling and less modularity.
